defaults.permitted_development: Across Cornwall, window and door work is usually simplest on the planning permission route when it stays close to like-for-like replacement and does not materially alter the size, position, appearance or privacy impact of existing openings. Prominent elevations and more exposed frontages can make appearance, detailing and visible material change matter more than a simple replacement assumption suggests.

rules.height_rules: Changing the height of openings or creating new upper-level windows is usually much more sensitive than routine replacement joinery.
rules.depth_rules: Projection, reveal depth and grouped opening changes can affect whether the work still reads as simple replacement rather than an elevation redesign.
rules.boundary_rules: Side-facing upper-floor windows, new front openings and privacy impacts often become the key local pressure points for this kind of work.
rules.roof_rules: If the project includes rooflights or roof-facing windows, it should be checked against the separate roof alteration route rather than treated as standard joinery replacement.
rules.materials_rules: Frame profile, colour, material and detailing can all matter where the building has a stronger architectural rhythm or a more sensitive setting.

rules.permitted_development: In Cornwall, window and door work is usually easiest to keep off the formal planning permission route when it stays close to like-for-like replacement and avoids new openings, stronger privacy impacts or a material change to the elevation. A like-for-like replacement rarely causes the same planning pressure as grouped opening changes, taller glazing or a visibly reworked entrance arrangement.

rules.height_rules: In Cornwall, new or enlarged openings that change the height of windows and doors are usually more sensitive than straightforward replacement joinery, especially at upper levels or on visible elevations.
rules.depth_rules: Projection, bay-style build-outs and grouped opening changes can make window and door work in Cornwall feel more like an elevation redesign than a simple replacement.
rules.boundary_rules: Privacy, side-facing upper-floor windows and visually assertive front-elevation changes are common local pressure points in Cornwall.
rules.roof_rules: Rooflights or roof-facing openings linked to a joinery project in Cornwall should usually be checked against the separate roof alteration route as well.
rules.materials_rules: Frame proportions, colour, material choice and overall appearance usually matter most in Cornwall where the building or street has a stronger character that the new joinery should still respect.

restrictions.conservation_area: Window and door changes in conservation areas within Cornwall often face tighter design control where they affect visible elevations or traditional detailing.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed buildings in Cornwall usually need listed building consent or a more careful heritage review before window and door changes are assumed to be straightforward.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions can matter for visible joinery changes in some areas, particularly where character-based controls remove the simpler fallback route.
